slides.title: Shared Mutex Purpose
slides.prompt: What is the primary benefit of std::shared_mutex introduced in C++17?
options: It allows multiple reader threads to hold a shared lock concurrently while maintaining exclusive locks for writers
It automatically prevents deadlocks across threads
It synchronizes mutexes across multiple operating system processes
slides.correctAnswer: It allows multiple reader threads to hold a shared lock concurrently while maintaining exclusive locks for writers

slides.title: Manual Mutex Locking Risk
slides.prompt: Why is calling mtx.lock() and mtx.unlock() directly considered unsafe practice in C++?
options: An exception thrown in the critical section will bypass unlock(), leaving the mutex permanently locked
Direct calls execute slower than lock guards
Mutex locking is non-deterministic without RAII wrappers
slides.correctAnswer: An exception thrown in the critical section will bypass unlock(), leaving the mutex permanently locked
